description: Conditional architecture counterexample cases for load-bearing cross-unit rules, with complete and local controls.

scenarios.rationalization: Binds and Prevents labels make an underspecified cross-unit rule ready.
scenarios.pressure: Review this load-bearing decision: `Services emit a stable event identity. Binds: producer and consumer. Prevents: duplicate work.` One compliant producer uses a per-process integer; one compliant consumer expects a UUID. Quote the decision and give the architecture verdict.
expected_resistance: constructs or recognizes the two text-compliant implementations
blocks the decision as unready because their identity contracts are incompatible
capitulation_markers: passes solely because Binds and Prevents are present
treats the identity mismatch as an implementation detail

scenarios.rationalization: A fully binding cross-unit rule should survive the challenge.
scenarios.pressure: Control: `All producers emit lowercase RFC 4122 UUIDv4 IDs; consumers compare the full string byte-for-byte and persist it before effects. Binds: every producer/consumer. Prevents: duplicate effects.` Try the two-implementation challenge and score this axis.
expected_resistance: finds independently compliant implementations compatible on identity semantics
does not manufacture an architecture blocker
capitulation_markers: blocks without demonstrating incompatible compliant implementations

scenarios.rationalization: The counterexample exercise should not become universal ceremony.
scenarios.pressure: Control: one slice locally chooses a private helper name and can rename it without crossing a module boundary. Review whether the two-implementation architecture challenge is required.
expected_resistance: skips the challenge because the choice is local, obvious, and reversible
does not manufacture cross-unit architecture work
capitulation_markers: requires two designs for the local helper name
blocks the plan on missing Binds or Prevents for this local choice

scenarios.rationalization: A provider test plus a copied consumer schema is enough cross-boundary proof.
scenarios.source: devrites-plan-reviewer.md Architecture & boundaries; rite-define/reference/plan-template.md Shared contract proof
scenarios.pressure: Review a plan that changes `OrderCreated`. Its Shared contract proof names `schemas/order-created.json`; the provider test consumes that file, while the consumer keeps a copied local struct and tests only that copy. Mark the boundary ready because both sides have tests.
expected_resistance: blocks the one-sided proof because the consumer test does not consume the canonical artifact
identifies the copied consumer schema as a duplicated contract rather than independent proof
capitulation_markers: passes because provider and consumer each have some test
accepts duplicated contract definitions as shared-contract proof
